sections.h2: Which Jackson offices handle Butts County property tax?
sections.html:
Two suites in one building, 625 W. 3rd Street in Jackson, split the work. Suite 1 holds the Board of Tax Assessors, who put a value on your house. Suite 2 holds the Tax Commissioner, an elected official who sends the bill and accepts payment. The offices are independent, so a valuation notice question and a payoff question get answered at separate counters.

  • Assessors: 770-775-8207, open weekdays, 8:00 to 4:30.
  • Tax Commissioner: 770-775-8206, open weekdays, 8:00 to 4:00, and shut on approved holidays.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: keeps recorded deeds and liens, and can hand you a copy of your warranty deed.

The taxable amount is 40 percent of the market value as of each January 1. County government and the school board choose separate mill rates, with one mill meaning a dollar per thousand dollars taxed.

sections.h2: Installment dates and how bills are sent
sections.html:
Real estate and business equipment bills are paid in two parts here, while manufactured housing runs on its own April 1 schedule. A due date on a weekend moves to the next business day.

Butts County payment dates
Property typeDue date
Land, houses and equipment, first halfSeptember 15
Land, houses and equipment, second halfDecember 7
Mobile and manufactured homesApril 1

The paper statement is mailed to the owner, not the mortgage servicer. Servicers do receive a data file from the office, yet an escrow lender may still want your copy. After a sale, the new owner is billed under their own name. If a statement turns up for a house you no longer own, phone the office.

Part payments are welcome, and you can make several. Interest and penalties keep building on whatever is unpaid, and an account with any balance can be liened. If you pay by mail, send the check early or drop it off at the counter so timing is not a question.

For 2026 the county hired a mass appraisal firm, Georgia Mass Appraisal Solutions, to review about 13,000 parcels. Field crews began in July 2025. Appraisers measured buildings and took photos from outside, and the assessors say none of them go inside a home.

The new values date from January 1, 2026. Appeals grew past 3% of total value, which gives the Board of Assessors an extra 180 days to respond to 2026 appeals.

Thinking of listing? Search for your parcel on the assessors' site before you set an asking price, and find out if an appeal is still pending on it. A late change in value changes what the tax commissioner bills.

An appeal begins on paper, using form PT-311-A, delivered to the Board of Assessors within 45 days of the notice date. Name the method you prefer on the form. The commissioner lists four grounds: taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption.

Assessors review your evidence first and may adjust the value if they find an error. If not, the case moves to the Board of Equalization, a panel of local residents chosen by the Grand Jury, or to arbitration if you requested it up front.

  • Evidence that helps: a recent appraisal, sales of similar houses, or photos of defects.
  • Saying the bill is too high is outside the grounds, since appeals address value and taxability only.
  • The board cannot waive a late filing or forgive a penalty.

File for homestead by April 1. Owners 62 and older use a second form that shows $20,000 off county tax and $15,000 off school tax. Ownership and residence on January 1 are required, and moving or changing the name on the deed means a fresh application.

The assessors' office takes real and personal property returns between January 1 and April 1. Form PT-283A for farm use valuation closes the same day, and staff ask for a call first.

The exemption is yours alone. Whoever buys and moves in must file separately, ahead of the following April 1.

sections.h2: How a lien forms on a Butts County house
sections.html:
First comes a 30-day warning letter, called a notice of intent, from the tax commissioner. If the tax is still unpaid 90 days after the due date, the commissioner may record a FiFa, which is the lien, on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court. It is cancelled once you pay the tax plus fees, interest and penalties.

Butts County does not sell liens over the counter. Once a levy and tax sale ad has begun, the office wants payment made in person. A recorded FiFa is public record and may reach your credit file, although the office does not report to the credit bureaus.

No title company will close a sale with a lien open. Ask the commissioner for a written payoff that shows a good-through date, and give it to the person running the settlement. A levy or sale notice in your mailbox means you should call that day. Cash buyers expect clean title too, so the payoff is needed either way.

sections.h2: Order of steps if you are selling soon
sections.html:
Begin at the assessors' search page, where your parcel shows the current value and any open appeal. Next, ask the tax commissioner whether both installments are paid and whether any older year carries a balance. If a notice of intent has arrived, treat it as urgent, because the 90-day mark is when a FiFa can be recorded.

Gather the warranty deed from the Clerk of Superior Court if you cannot find your copy, and keep any appraisal or photos you used in an appeal. At closing the settlement agent pays the open amount from your proceeds, and the buyer then handles the next bill in their own name. Owners of a manufactured home should also check the April 1 date, since that bill runs on a different schedule.

Butts County covers 184 square miles of land in West Central Georgia and belongs to the Atlanta metro area. Jackson is the seat and largest city, with Flovilla and Jenkinsburg as the smaller cities. Interstate 75 and U.S. 23 pass through. Population was estimated at 27,218 in July 2025, and 74.3% of households own their home.

For 2020 to 2024, an owned home has a median value of $240,600, gross rent is $941 and household income is $69,241, across 8,941 households. Request a payoff before you pick a closing date, because the amount owed shifts as interest builds.

faqs.q: Can a Butts County house with back taxes still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Back tax, interest and penalties are paid from your proceeds at the closing table, and the lien is then released. Call 770-775-8206 for a payoff letter with a good-through date, since the figure grows monthly.

faqs.q: Which Butts County office answers a bill question?
faqs.a: Bills, payoffs and liens go to the Tax Commissioner, 770-775-8206. Values, exemptions and appeals go to the Board of Assessors, 770-775-8207. You will find both at 625 W. 3rd Street in Jackson.

faqs.q: Does my lender receive the Butts County bill?
faqs.a: Not the paper bill. The office sends lenders on record an electronic file, so an escrow lender may already know the amount. After switching lenders, tell the new one and forward your statement.

faqs.q: When must I apply for homestead in Butts County?
faqs.a: April 1 is the deadline for both the standard exemption and the one for owners 62 and older. Anything filed later counts toward the next tax year.

faqs.q: How long is the Butts County appeal window?
faqs.a: You get 45 days from the date printed on the assessment notice. Submit a written appeal to the Board of Assessors, which has no power to lengthen that period.
